info.title: MemberSuite REST API
info.description:
The MemberSuite REST API exposes the association management system as one deployable web app per
feature module. Every module shares the conventions below.

### Authentication

All endpoints except `/about` require an `Authorization` header carrying an access token. Requests
without one are rejected with **401**, as are requests whose token lacks the security rights for the
record being touched — check both the token and the user's security settings when you see a 401.

### Tenants

Routes ending in `{tenantid}` are scoped to a single association. The tenant id is the numeric
association identifier, and it must match the partition the token was issued for. Routes that take an
`{id}` instead resolve the tenant from the record itself.

### Searching

Collection endpoints take an MSQL statement in `msql`, plus `page` (zero-based) and `pageSize`.
MSQL is MemberSuite's SQL-like query language, for example:

    SELECT ID, Name FROM Committee WHERE IsActive = true ORDER BY Name

A search returns only the fields the statement selects, not the full record. To discover the fields
and validation rules for a type, call its `/description/{tenantid}` endpoint.

### Creating and updating

* **POST** creates a record. Do **not** send `id` or `systemTimestamp` — either one makes the request
  fail with **409 Conflict**. Audit fields (`createdBy`, `createdDate`, `lastModifiedBy`,
  `lastModifiedDate`) are assigned by the server and ignored if supplied. A successful create returns
  **201** with the new `id` and a `Location` header.
* **PUT** replaces a record in full. Any field you omit is cleared, so read the record first and send
  it back with your changes applied. If you include `id` it must match the id in the URI.
* **DELETE** removes a record by id.

### Custom fields

Associations add their own fields to most objects, and those fields do **not** appear in the schemas
below - the schema shows the standard fields only. Send a custom field as a top-level property named
after the field itself, alongside the standard ones:

    { "name": "Finance Committee", "isActive": true, "MeetingRoom__c": "Boardroom" }

Call the object's `/description/{tenantid}` endpoint to discover which custom fields an association
has configured and what type each expects. A custom field of type Document or Image is sent under
`<FieldName>_Contents` instead, as an object carrying `filecontents` (base-64), `filename` and
`filetype`.

### Concurrency and caching

Endpoints that return a single record support conditional requests: send the `etag` from a previous
response back in `If-None-Match` and you will get **304** if nothing has changed. An update that
collides with someone else's change returns **409** — re-read the record and retry.

### Long-running requests

Send `Asynchronous: true` on a POST, PUT or DELETE to queue the work instead of waiting. The response
is **202 Accepted** with a `Location` header pointing at
`/{module}/v{version}/asyncstatus/{id}`, which you can poll for the outcome.

### Media types

Requests and responses are JSON with camel-cased property names. Ask for `application/hal+json` to
receive HATEOAS `_links` alongside each record.

get.summary: Reports the health and build of the Certifications REST service.
get.description:
Requires no access token, so it is safe to use as a load balancer health check. The response carries the
            running assembly version and its build timestamp, and lists the XML documentation files Swagger loaded its
            descriptions from - an empty list there means this deployment is publishing an undocumented API.

get.summary: Reports the outcome of an asynchronous operation.
get.description:
When a request is sent with an Asynchronous: true header the API answers 202 Accepted and a
            Location header pointing here. Poll this endpoint until it stops reporting Pending: once the
            work succeeds it answers 303 See Other with a Location header addressing the finished record,
            and if the work failed it answers 500 carrying the error.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Identifier of the queued operation, taken from the Location header of the 202 response.

303.description: The operation succeeded. The Location header addresses the resulting record.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

404.description: No operation exists with that id.

500.description: The operation failed. The body carries the error.

get.summary: Lists the certification applications an applicant already has in progress.
get.description:
Use it before starting a new application, so an applicant is offered their existing draft rather than
            a duplicate. Omit the applicant to list every application in the association.

parameters.name: applicantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the applicant. Omit to list applications for everyone.

400.description: The applicant id could not be read.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

post.summary: Submits a certification application, reporting what is missing if it is not ready.
post.description: Checks the application against the requirements of its programme first. If anything is outstanding the application is not submitted and the unmet requirements come back so they can be shown to the applicant; if everything is satisfied it is submitted. Prefer this over application/submitApplication, which submits without the pre-check.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the application to submit.

parameters.name: sendConfirmationEmailOnSuccess
parameters.description: Whether to email the applicant when the submission succeeds.

200.description: Either the submitted application, or the requirements still outstanding.

400.description: The application id could not be read.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

404.description: No application exists with that id.

get.description:
Returns the manifest for one exam assignment rule - the candidates due to sit that exam at that
            location - which is what an exam invigilator needs on the day.

parameters.name: certificationApplicationExamAssignmentRuleId
parameters.description: Identifier of the exam assignment rule.

400.description: The rule id could not be read.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

404.description: No exam assignment rule exists with that id.

post.summary: Builds the order for a certification application's own fees.
post.description:
Creates the order covering the application and exam fees the programme charges, ready to be paid
            through the Orders module. Use application/generateOrderBasedOnCertificationAdditionalFees for
            fees that come from an additional fee rule set instead.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the application to raise fees for.

400.description: The application id could not be read.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

404.description: No application exists with that id.

post.summary: Builds an order for the additional fees a rule set applies to a certification application.
post.description:
Covers charges beyond the programme's standard application fee - late fees, retakes, materials -
            as defined by the rule set you name. Separate from
            application/generateOrderForCertificationApplication, which raises the standard fees, so an
            applicant may end up with more than one order.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the application to raise fees for.

parameters.name: ruleSetId
parameters.description: Identifier of the additional fee rule set to apply.

400.description: An id could not be read.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

404.description: The application or rule set does not exist.

post.summary: Emails a recommender again, asking them to complete their recommendation.
post.description:
Sends the recommendation request afresh to the recommender named on the record - the nudge to send
            when an applicant is waiting on someone. Every call sends another email.

400.description: The recommendation id could not be read.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

404.description: No recommendation exists with that id.

post.summary: Records a recommender's completed recommendation for a certification application.
post.description:
This is the endpoint behind the form a recommender fills in after being sent a request by
            application/resendRecommendationNotice. Submitting a recommendation may satisfy one of the
            application's requirements, so re-check it with application/tryToSubmitCertificationApplication
            afterwards.

400.description: The payload was missing or could not be parsed.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

404.description: The application named on the recommendation does not exist.

post.summary: Submits a certification application without checking its requirements first.
post.description:
Submits the application as it stands. Unlike
            application/tryToSubmitCertificationApplication it does not verify that the programme's
            requirements are met and it sends no confirmation email, so prefer that endpoint for anything
            applicant-facing and keep this one for staff overrides.

parameters.description: Identifier of the application to submit.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

404.description: No application exists with that id.

get.summary: Lists the association's active certification programme categories.
get.description:
The top level of the certification catalogue. Use a category id from here to narrow
            application/certificationPrograms. Only active categories are returned.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: Identifier of the association whose categories should be listed.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

get.summary: Lists the active certification programmes on offer.
get.description:
Returns the programmes someone may apply for, narrowed to one category if you name one. Programmes
            are offered either to individuals or to organisations and the two sets differ, so
            applicableTo decides which catalogue you see - it defaults to individuals.

parameters.name: applicableTo
parameters.description: Whether to list programmes for individuals or for organisations. Defaults to individuals.

parameters.name: categoryId
parameters.description: Restricts the list to one programme category. Omit for all of them.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

get.summary: Describes the application processes defined for a certification programme.
get.description:
A programme may define more than one route to the same certification - a first application and a
            renewal, for instance - and each is a separate process with its own steps. Pick one and pass its id to
            application/createApplication to start an application. Narrow by type when you already
            know which route you want.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Restricts the result to one kind of process. Omit for all of them.

400.description: The programme id could not be read.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

404.description: No programme exists with that id.

post.summary: Starts a certification application by creating an empty one from a process.
post.description:
Creates the application record and returns it with the workflow the applicant now works through. Check
            application/getAllExistingApplications first, so an applicant with a draft already open is not
            given a second one.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: Identifier of the application process to start.

400.description: The process id could not be read.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

404.description: No application process exists with that id.

get.summary: Returns the portal workflow an applicant fills in, step by step.
get.description:
Describes the steps and the fields on each, so a portal can render the application form without
            knowing what the association configured. Use application/determineNextApplicationStep to decide
            where the applicant goes next.

parameters.name: workflowId
parameters.description: Identifier of the workflow instance to describe.

parameters.name: replaceNullSideLabel
parameters.description: Whether to substitute a default label where a field has none. Defaults to true.

400.description: The workflow id could not be read.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

404.description: No workflow exists with that id.

get.summary: Works out which step of an application the applicant should see next.
get.description:
Steps are not always taken in order: a process can skip steps that do not apply to this applicant, so
            ask this rather than incrementing the step number yourself.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the application in progress.

parameters.name: currentStep
parameters.description: The step the applicant has just completed.

400.description: The application id or step could not be read.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

404.description: No application exists with that id.

post.summary: Lists the application steps that still have required fields unanswered.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifier of the application to check.

post.summary: Renders CEU transcripts for everyone matching a filter, and returns a link to them.
post.description:
The bulk counterpart of certifications/printCEUTranscript, which covers only the
            signed-in user. Supply an MSQL filter clause selecting the credit holders you want.
            <para>
            The filter may not constrain Owner: a clause containing Owner = or
            Owner IN ( is rejected, because the owner is fixed to the caller's own identity by the
            server. Filter on other fields instead.
            </para>

parameters.name: request
parameters.description: The MSQL filter clause selecting whose transcripts to render.

400.description: The filter was missing, empty, or attempted to constrain Owner.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

post.summary: Renders the signed-in user's own CEU transcript.
post.description:
The transcript is always the caller's own - the individual is taken from the portal user on the
            access token, and there is no way to ask for someone else's. Use
            certifications/printCEUTranscriptByFilter for that.
            <para>
            Supply both dates to limit the transcript to credits earned in that window; supply neither for
            the full history. Supplying only one is the same as supplying neither.
            </para>

parameters.name: creditStartDate
parameters.description: Earliest credit date to include. Only honoured together with the end date.

parameters.name: creditEndDate
parameters.description: Latest credit date to include. Only honoured together with the start date.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

404.description: The access token carries no portal user, so there is no transcript to render.
